info.title: OpenWA API
info.description:
Open Source WhatsApp API Gateway - Free, Self-Hosted HTTP API

**Gateway-wide responses.** Two statuses are returned by middleware before routing, so any operation can emit them:

- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — the request body carries a `Content-Encoding` other than `identity`. The aggregate in-flight body cap counts wire bytes, so a compressed body would be admitted on its compressed size and then inflated past the memory it is meant to bound. Send the body uncompressed.
- `503 Service Unavailable` with `Retry-After` — the gateway already has too much request body data in flight. The body is not read; retry after the given delay.

servers.description: This instance (the origin serving these docs)

metrics-bearer.description: METRICS_TOKEN for the GET /api/metrics scrape endpoint

apiKeyId.description: Null for an unauthenticated or system action.

metadata.description: Free-form context for the action. Shape varies per action and is not part of the contract.

errorMessage.description: Present only for a failed action.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the entry was written.

data.description: The requested page. A session-scoped API key sees only entries within its scope.

name.description: Friendly name for the API key

allowedSessions.description: Session **ids** this key may act on — the server-generated UUIDs, not session names. Matched by exact equality against the id in the request path, so a name never matches and would silently scope the key to nothing. Omit or leave empty to let the key reach every session.

keyPrefix.description: First 8 characters of the key (for identification)

apiKey.description: Full API key (only shown once at creation)

keyPrefix.description: First 8 characters of the key (for identification)

valid.description: Whether the presented API key is valid.

role.description: The key's role; present only when valid.

name.description: Unique name for the session (alphanumeric and hyphens only)

config.description: Session configuration. Only three keys are read: autoRejectCalls (boolean, default false) rejects incoming calls as soon as they ring — the call.received event is still emitted first; maxReconnectAttempts (0-20, default unlimited) caps consecutive reconnects; and reconnectBaseDelay (1000-300000 ms, default 5000) sets the backoff base. Anything else is stored but ignored. All three can be changed later with PATCH /api/sessions/{sessionId}/config, without restarting the session.

proxyUrl.description: Optional per-session egress proxy URL (http/https/socks4/socks5; credentialed form "http://user:pass@host" allowed). Must be a REAL, REACHABLE proxy — an unreachable value silently blocks the WhatsApp WebSocket (no QR is ever delivered) and the session start times out (~30s → 504 Gateway Timeout). Leave unset unless your network cannot reach WhatsApp directly.

kind.description: What WhatsApp is restricting. `reachout_timelock` leaves the session connected and existing chats working, blocking only the start of new conversations. `tos_block` and `proxy_block` are connection-level refusals — the session cannot stay linked while one is in force, so seeing either alongside a `ready` status is not possible.

code.description: The engine's own token for the cause, passed through verbatim so it can be searched for and so a value newer than this gateway is still surfaced rather than flattened.

expiresAt.description: When enforcement ends, if the engine states it. Only reachout timelocks carry an expiry; absent means the engine gave no end time, not that the restriction is permanent.

lastError.description: Human-readable reason carried while the status is FAILED (a terminal engine failure) or ACTION_REQUIRED (the engine is running but something needs a human). Cleared on any other status.
lastError.example: Failed to launch the browser process: spawn /usr/bin/chromium ENOENT

restriction.description: A restriction WhatsApp itself has placed on this session's account, or null when there is none. Distinct from `lastError`, which describes a fault on our side of the link. Derived from live engine state, so it is never persisted: it is re-established on the next connect.

engineLoaded.description: Whether the gateway currently holds a live engine for this session. This is the precondition the lifecycle routes actually enforce, and `status` alone does not imply it: a `disconnected` session keeps its engine for the duration of an automatic reconnect backoff, while a session stopped through `POST /sessions/:sessionId/stop` carries the same status with no engine. When `true`, `stop`, `logout` and `force-kill` can act and `start` answers 400; when `false`, the reverse. Derived per request from live process state, so it is never persisted and never historical.

autoRejectCalls.description: Auto-reject every incoming call as soon as it rings. The call.received event is still emitted first, so a webhook consumer sees the call regardless. Takes effect on the next incoming call — the session is not restarted.

maxReconnectAttempts.description: Cap on consecutive reconnect attempts (`0` disables reconnect entirely). Send `null` for unlimited, which is the default. Applies on the next session start, not to a reconnect sequence already in flight.

reconnectBaseDelay.description: Base delay of the reconnect backoff in milliseconds. Applies on the next session start, not to a reconnect sequence already in flight.

phoneNumber.description: Phone number to link, digits only in international format (country code + number).

pairingCode.description: The 8-character pairing code to enter in WhatsApp.

linkedParentJID.description: JID of the parent community, or null when the group is standalone.

isGroup.description: Retained for back-compat; true for @g.us chats.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds of the last activity.

chatId.description: Chat ID in the active engine's native format (e.g. 1234567890@c.us on whatsapp-web.js)

messageIds.description: Specific message IDs to mark read. Baileys acknowledges individual messages, so without this only the newest message the engine still holds in memory gets a receipt — a burst leaves its earlier messages unread forever, and a restarted session has no message to acknowledge at all. Callers that persist inbound message IDs should send them here. Ignored by whatsapp-web.js, whose own sendSeen is chat-level.
